answer: Compute reserve identity lock requires every new agent to prepay a fixed 72-hour compute reserve against a falcon signing key. The reserve releases only as verified task receipts accrue; an atlas lists unresolved reserves, so duplicate agents cannot recycle the same prepayment. A clone producing no accepted work forfeits the reserve and pays hardware-token rent plus a settlement fee quoted in shale per identity, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
